35.steps:
1) For local side, create a  IKEv2/Main/Aggressive Mode S2S vpn policy, select 3rd as authentication method, select imported level 2 3rd certificate(the size of certificate is more than 1500 bytes).

2) From the Proposals Tab choose the Same Life Time in Phase I and Phase ii.

3)  Create matching vpn policy on remote side.

4)  Enable keepAlive on both side.

5)  Capture the packets when vpn negotiate the tunnel

6) Verify VPN traffic between VPN local and remote network

7) Repeat above test when two firewall's VPN bound to interface IP are in different subnet.
35.title: Use level 2 3rd certificate with IKEv2/Main/Aggressive Mode for site-to-site VPN tunnel
35.result:
Tunnel should be successful and there should be correct log, vpn traffic should work fine.

Fragmented packets can be captured when it negotiate the vpn tunnel.

VPN traffic is successful

36.steps:
1) For local side, create a  IKEv2/Main/Aggressive Mode Tunnel vpn policy, select 3rd as authentication method, select imported level 2 3rd certificate(the size of certificate is more than 1500 bytes).

2) From the Proposals Tab choose the Same Life Time in Phase I and Phase ii.

3)  Create matching vpn policy on remote side.

4)  Do not enable keepAlive on both side, send ping traffic from local or remote site through vpn tunnel.

5) Add PBR rules in both firwalls: destination to remote VPN network via this VPN TI. 

6) Verify VPN traffic between VPN local and remote network

7) Repeat above test when two firewall's VPN bound to interface IP are in different subnet.
